newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Wellington National candidate resolves to stay.
newsitem.headline: Wellington National candidate resolves to stay.

text.p: A rebel group within the ruling National Party on Monday urged its own candidate in Wellington Central to stand aside to ensure a win for one of its likely coalition partners.
But National's candidate Mark Thomas is refusing to step down in favour of ACT leader and former Labour cabinet minister Richard Prebble, and instead suggested ACT should withdraw from the election.
"It is for the voters to decide who their MP will be, not political manipulators," Thomas told Reuters.
The Wellington Central seat is becoming a key battleground in the October 12 election, with the potential to determine the make-up of the government after the October 12 election.

ACT is averaging 3.8 percent nationwide party support in recent opinion polls and, unless it attracts five percent of the party vote, must win an electorate seat in order to qualify for its share of the seats in parliament.
Prebble, who has been a close third behind Thomas and Labour's Alick Shaw in polls in the seat, is seen as the best chance for the party to win an electorate.

National is averaging 38.5 percent in nationwide polling. It would need to increase its support and have both ACT and the moral conservative Christian Coalition, polling just over the five percent threshold, represented in parliament to be confident of re-election.

Thomas told Reuters he was sure the the group asking him to stand down were ACT supporters. He said his campaign team was countering the call by seeking a legal opinion on whether ACT could withdraw from the race leaving the field open for National.
"Their four percent is preventing a centre-right government," he said.
"Candidates can't withdraw...but the (Electoral) Act is ambiguous on whether a party can be struck off (the ballot paper)," Thomas said.
He said ACT had failed despite an aggressive advertising campaign and would go down in history as "the most expensive political failure".

Thomas said he had the support of party president Geoff Thompson and Prime Minister Jim Bolger to continue. He conceded there were others in the party who had a different view, but said it was "too late in the piece to be considering it".
National opted not to stand a candidate in the Ohariu- Belmont seat to help its coalition partner United win, but has refused deals for its other potential allies.
